newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DHL says E.Europe to grow more strongly.
newsitem.headline: DHL says E.Europe to grow more strongly.

text.p: Express distribution company DHL Worldwide Express said on Friday it expected a "second push" of growth in its business in former communist Europe that will exceed its performance in the last five years.
"Since 1992, our growth has been tremendous with our turnover increasing sixfold," Peter Davies, DHL's director for central and eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, told Reuters.

"This was during an initial euphoria about the region, which has plateaued a little now," he said. "But there will be a second push starting in a couple of years that will be fantastic. Our business will accelerate even faster than it has in the past five years."
Davies declined to disclose additional details.
The revival would come after governments in the region cleared away the lingering remnants of 40 years of communism, Davies said.

"Once some governments realize they can't cling to their previous beliefs, we can really start to push forward," he said. "This already has begun to happen in Bulgaria, where a socialist goverment has been replaced by conservative leaders committed to privatisation and overall economic development."
DHL, which already has invested roughly $160 million in former communist Europe, plans to invest another $18 million a year until 2000 to prepare for the expected growth in business, Davies said.

"We are investing to complete the infrastructure and technology required to create solid, stable and professional orgainisations throughout the region," he said. "The art is for us to determine when and where the growth will happen to match our resources to the increasing demand."
